title: beforeSearch hook
body:
What about providing a `beforeSearch(helper)` hook that would be responsible one provided for launching the helper.search() method?

It would solve cases like:
- I want to programmatically add filters based on the query: if the query changes, I want to update optional facet filters (cc @olance)
- I want to avoid doing the first search query #4 
- avoid search if chars.length < X #185 #182 
- debounce the searchbox #776 #817 (only issue being you do not know it was triggered by the searchBox, but should be enough)
- Let the developer choose to trigger the search (not sure fully resolved by this proposal) #769 

The naming might not be the best one, other possiblities:
- searchHook
- ??

``` js
instantsearch(appID, apiKey, {
  searchHook: function(helper) {
    // once you define the search hook, it's your responsability to call helper.search, otherwise: no search is done
  }
})
```

comments.body:
Solves everything!(tm) The proposed API is a bit raw, though. Why not make that an event? And like DOM events, provide a function that would let stop the behavior? (and lets retrigger it).

Otherwise seems great :+1:

> Solves everything!(tm)

I am pretty sure it does not :D Someone will come and say "YES BUT.."

An event would be way better indeed :+1: 
Why not have it return falsy/truthy and test that to check if the search should continue?

I don't see the point in introducing a function just for stopping the search in our case.

> An event would be way better indeed

Why/How would it be better?

> Why not have it return falsy/truthy and test that to check if the search should continue?

That's what I planned at the begining but I always found those kind of APIS less obvious than just calling "helper.search"

Warning this do not means you would be able to easily do the "render on server, cancel first query" Because rendering on server would not make the facets value clickable. They would not yet be binded.

I believe if one use would really want to implement a full server-side - bind on frontend, it would require us to work on #833 a lot more.

cc @hkdobrev you will find the proposal to solve both initial query and search debounce in the first comment.

See https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/issues/823#issuecomment-183356773 to understand that having a full server side rendering AND using instantsearch.js to rebind server-generated facet values is not currently feasible, if you have any idea how we would do so, let me know.

Also cc @VonD

> > An event would be way better indeed
> > Why/How would it be better?

I think it's better because it allows you to add different hooks from different places, and setting a hook by using events means you're not replacing someone else's hook! (which is the case if you have to do `thing.beforeHook = ...`)

> I think it's better because it allows you to add different hooks from different places

Well having configuration for hooks in multiple places might lead to poorly understandable behavior. For example if you have two hooks set in different places you won't necessarily know exactly what the other one is doing. If both try to do the same thing (like a debounce) it can be pretty messy.

:+1: on your proposition @vvo to have two API's

> Well having configuration for hooks in multiple places might lead to poorly understandable behavior. For example if you have two hooks set in different places you won't necessarily know exactly what the other one is doing. If both try to do the same thing (like a debounce) it can be pretty messy.

I agree, but that's something you should leave to the developer.
I have had problems with that kind of decisions being made for me in the past. Forcing a single hook can be in some situations very difficult to work with. When several event hooks can be registered, you have more flexibility and you can decide what's OK to do and what's not depending on your own context.

I am not sure I agree with the complexity of having two methods introduced.  
I see this `beforeSearch` hook just as a "before filter" in Rails: you can register several filters that will be called one after the other before a controller action takes place; any of the filters can return false/raise an exception/trigger a redirect, which will block the default execution flow.

An analogy that could make more sense here are the middlewares in Express.js for instance.  
Why should we separate this logic into two different methods/hooks when you can have a single one?

Call the hooks in the order they were registered. Each hook can change the helper config and do just that, and others can prevent search execution by returning false or calling a special function (I'd prefer returning false but that's another point).  
I can't see the need for a special function that would replace the search logic?

> An analogy that could make more sense here are the middlewares in Express.js for instance.

Yes what you describe are middlewares: functions able to cancel or continue the flow of others. But it seems a bit overkill here?

For example, how would you implement debouncing with your solution?

@olance We cannot implement the return true/false pattern. This is not a common JavaScript pattern in APIS.

Most of the time when you have events, no code will listen to the return value of the event handler.

@vvo This is just an implementation detail. If you want to separate into two API methods you can do that; if you want to have more of a middleware concept, which I think is a more elegant solution, whether it checks that each middleware returned true/false or called a callback you provided is up to you.

Plus, the return pattern is a very simple way to achieve what we want, and easily documented too (`return false if you want to cancel the current search`), and no-one is actually going to need to "listen" to the return value but your own internal code. So to me that's not that big of an issue.

In the end, for a start, I will go for the initial proposal that can solve the needs and do not require too much new API entries.

If you really need to split your hook in multiple functions that will be still feasible, on your side. Using any middleware library or your own.

We will see how people use this and iterate if needed.

Exposing a single function should be ok in most cases.
OK, the simpler the better, let's start with that :) :+1:
